what_its_for: Carisoprodol is a muscle relaxer used for short-term relief of muscle pain and discomfort caused by strains, sprains, or other muscle injuries. It works by blocking pain signals between your nerves and your brain. It is usually used along with rest, physical therapy, and other treatments.
how_to_take: Take carisoprodol exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Do not take more than prescribed and do not take it for longer than 2 to 3 weeks unless your doctor tells you to. This medicine can be habit-forming, so never share it with anyone else.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 350 mg taken three times a day and at bedtime. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store carisoprodol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking carisoprodol. Alcohol can increase drowsiness and dizziness and raise your risk of serious side effects. Avoid driving a car, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medications, opioid pain relievers, or antihistamines, unless your doctor approves.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: a seizure, extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up, fast or pounding heartbeat, trouble breathing, severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue), confusion, agitation, or loss of coordination. Also contact your doctor if you feel dependent on the medication or if your muscle pain does not improve.
when_it_works: Carisoprodol usually starts working within 30 minutes of taking it. You may feel relief from muscle pain and stiffness fairly quickly. It is only meant to be used for short periods of time, typically no longer than 2 to 3 weeks, because there is not enough evidence that it works well for long-term use and it can become habit-forming.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): This medication is generally NOT recommended for older adults because it increases the risk of falls, confusion, and excessive sedation. Talk to your doctor about safer options. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Carisoprodol may harm an unborn baby. Breastfeeding: This medicine passes into breast milk and may cause drowsiness in a nursing infant. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Carisoprodol is not approved for use in children under 16 years of age. Kidney or liver problems: Use with caution. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or choose a different treatment.
